newsitem.title: LESOTHO: Lesotho's ruling party sacks ailing leader.
newsitem.headline: Lesotho's ruling party sacks ailing leader.

text.p: Lesotho Prime Minister Ntsu Mokhehle, who last month faced a police mutiny which was finally quelled by force, has been sacked by his party after accusations the country was drifting into lawlessness.
The ruling Basotholand Congress Party (BCP) resolved at a general conference on Sunday "to relieve Dr Ntsu Mokhehle of his leadership of the BCP with immediate effect".
Diplomats said BCP deputy leader Matlejane Qhobela was now entitled to become prime minister under the party's constitution, ahead of current Deputy Prime Minister Pakalitha Mosisili.
Mokhehle, 78, has not yet publicly reacted to the announcement.

Qhobela, who is not in Mokhehle's cabinet, is believed to lead a pressure group in the ruling party which has been lobbying for a leadership change ahead of a general election scheduled for next year.
"There might be political instability in the jockeying for position," one diplomat said.

"It has the potential for abuse (of democracy) but we would hope that they would follow the democratic process and go along with the constitution of Lesotho and of the party in electing a new leader," the diplomat told Reuters.
King Letsie III was expected to call a meeting of the southern African country's Council of State to deal with the leadership crisis, but no date had been set.

Despite the internal party wrangling and his poor health, diplomats said Mokhehle retained strong support from voters and party members during his term in office and was not necessarily a spent force.
Mokhehle has weathered a series of crises since March 1993 when he won the first democratic polls in two decades.
Last month Lesotho army troops ended an 11-day police mutiny, overwhelming the rebels with a dawn onslaught of heavy gunfire.
